A small release: Codex tried on real work, the docs' gaps for installing Deckhand closed, and
a security fix in the runner. It also brings run data on the dashboard, the Board's backlog by
milestone, a limit on auto-pickup, and replies on the pull request once a run has one. No
setting is renamed and nothing in your server folder or `.env` needs to change.

Every image is published for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`, tagged `0.2.0`, `0.2` and
`latest`, at `ghcr.io/bryansmee/deckhand-<service>`. The Helm chart (`deploy/helm/deckhand`)
is `0.2.0`, and its `appVersion` is `0.2.0`, at this tag.

## Security: branch images only from the repository's own commits

[GHSA-cwgw-fr6h-259p](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/security/advisories/GHSA-cwgw-fr6h-259p)
affects v0.1.0 and earlier. The runner trusted the orchestrator's word that a branch image was
built from the repository's own branch, so a compromised orchestrator could have it build a
fork's Dockerfile. Now the runner builds a branch's image only at a full commit id, after it
asks the github service whether that commit is the repository's own
([#1024](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1024)). Only repositories with the
`branch_docker_images` grant build branch images. Update the runner and the github service
together, as Compose and the chart already do: see [Runs in flight](#runs-in-flight).

## Codex, tried

Codex built two of Deckhand's own features on its own: the release mode
([#1061](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1061)) and run data
([#1059](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1059)). Both ran at about Claude Code's
speed, and its one `needs-input` stop pointed at a real gap in the issue. Two issues are a
first look, not a benchmark:
[How it does](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/blob/v0.2.0/docs/guides/codex.md#how-it-does)
([#1063](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1063)). Claude Code stays the default.

## New in the docs

- **A public App across several organizations**: a private App installs only on the account
  that owns it. Set `ALLOWED_REPOS` first, then make the App public and install it on each
  organization. Installations outside `ALLOWED_REPOS` get no runs and no replies:
  [Installing it on several organizations](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/blob/v0.2.0/docs/guides/github-app.md#installing-it-on-several-organizations)
  ([#1051](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1051)).
- **A stable tunnel** when the server has no public address. Tailscale Funnel was tested end
  to end. The cloudflared named tunnel and the ngrok static domain follow those tools' docs and
  are marked as not yet tested with Deckhand:
  [A tunnel when the server has no public address](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/blob/v0.2.0/docs/guides/tunnels.md)
  ([#1052](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1052)).
- **Choosing who reviews**: a review is already a fresh run. A repository's `review` block can
  have another agent (`agent: codex`) or a stronger model (`model: opus`) review the work:
  [Choosing who reviews](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/blob/v0.2.0/docs/repo-config/reviews.md#choosing-who-reviews)
  ([#1064](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1064)).

## What changed for your runs

- **Replies go on the pull request** once a work run's issue has an open one, whichever of
  the two the comment came from. The issue gets a short pointer that quotes the reply's first
  line. The `needs-input` label stays on the issue, and the boxes ticked in the pull request's
  reply answer it ([#1054](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1054),
  [Replies](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/blob/v0.2.0/docs/contributing/replies.md)).
- **Recordings of the tested flow**: the sandbox image has `img2webp`. On UI changes, the
  agent can join its screenshots into an animated WebP, which GitHub shows inline and moving
  ([#1050](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1050)). No new upload format: the broker
  already took WebP.
- **`auto_pickup_max_ready: <n>`** in `.deckhand.yaml`: auto-pickup takes none of a
  repository's issues while it has `n` or more of Deckhand's pull requests ready for review.
  It picks again soon after one is merged or closed. Unset, there is no limit, as before
  ([#1049](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1049),
  [Auto-pickup](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/blob/v0.2.0/docs/repo-config/issues.md)).
- **An exited sandbox's output is read again** after a failed read (up to 3 times) instead of
  ending the run with "No result". Codex's sandboxes, which exit as soon as they print, hit
  this most ([#1056](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1056)).
- **The orchestrator's start catch-up** (the repositories' listing, the pull requests, the
  redeliveries, the needs-input labels) now also runs when edge comes up after the
  orchestrator and the App is learned late
  ([#1062](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1062)).

## On the dashboard

- **Run data**: a repository's settings and a pull request task have a Run data tab. It
  compares retained runs by agent, model, effort, triggering user and repository: tokens and
  runs per issue, needs-input stops, review findings, fix runs and outcomes. Summaries saved
  before this release have no usage, user or push data, and show as unknown, never as zero
  ([#1059](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1059),
  [Run data](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/blob/v0.2.0/docs/guides/dashboard.md#run-data)).
- **Group by milestone** on the Board's backlog: a section per milestone, by due date, each
  one collapsible ([#1058](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1058)).

## For contributors

- A `release` mode for this repository drafts each release's checklist, its chart bump and
  these notes. Publishing stays with the maintainer
  ([#1061](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1061),
  [Cutting a release](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/blob/v0.2.0/docs/contributing/releases.md)).
- Files over 800 lines (1,500 for tests) can't grow: `test/file-sizes.test.mjs` holds them to
  their size on `main` ([#1073](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1073)).
- Two flaky tests fixed at their cause ([#1020](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1020),
  [#1062](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1062)), and the switch-time settings for
  the public repository recorded ([#1017](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1017)).

## Updating

No setting, grant or stored state changes, and none of the
[upgrade notes](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/blob/v0.2.0/docs/guides/upgrade-notes.md)
is new since v0.1.0. Update as usual
([Updating](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/blob/v0.2.0/docs/guides/updating.md)):

```sh
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
```

`docker compose pull` also takes the new sandbox image, which has `img2webp`. An updater that
only follows running containers (Watchtower) doesn't, because the `sandbox` service exits at
once: run `docker compose pull sandbox` yourself. On Kubernetes, take the chart or the base at
this tag.

## Runs in flight

Every merged pull request since v0.1.0 has a Runs in flight section. One case can break, and
only during the update:

- **Branch image builds while the runner is newer than the github service**
  ([#1024](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1024)). The new runner asks the github
  service whether a branch's commit is the repository's own (`GET /commits/…`), and a v0.1.0
  github service answers 403. The build then fails at once with "the github service: 403 for
  whether … is …'s own commit (one older than this runner doesn't answer it: update it)", and
  the run doesn't start. Default-branch builds and running sandboxes aren't affected. What to
  do: update every service together (`docker compose up -d`, or the chart or base at this
  tag), then trigger the run again.

The other cases need nothing:

- **Running sandboxes under the new services**: no sandbox variable, endpoint, token claim or
  proxy answer changed. The runner now cuts an incomplete output stream, which the older and
  the new orchestrator both treat as its end
  ([#1056](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1056)).
- **New runs on an older sandbox image**: they keep the old prompt and have no `img2webp`
  ([#1050](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1050)). Their replies still move to the
  pull request, but the agent doesn't know that their first line is quoted on the issue
  ([#1054](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1054)).
- **Runs the new orchestrator picks up**: their stored state is read as before, `replyTo`
  included ([#1054](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1054)). A Codex run that
  resumed its session across the update counts that session's whole token total once in run
  data ([#1059](https://github.com/BryanSmee/deckhand/pull/1059)). Nothing stored is
  rewritten.
